text: In California, a ballot that’s torn or too damaged for the scanner to read gets thrown out.
seenIn: a reply under an election video

room.label: students (demo crowd)
room.note: No published poll has measured this belief yet. The 5C pilot survey replaces this split with real student answers.

truthSource.label: California Secretary of State: Vote Counting Process
truthSource.oneLine: Ballots that are damaged or can’t be machine-read are remade by elections officials and processed with other ballots after Election Day.

lesson.pattern: The machine isn’t the last word
lesson.tip: A scanner rejecting a ballot is not the same as a vote being rejected. Officials remake damaged or unreadable ballots so the choices can be counted. When a post says ballots were “kicked out by the machine,” ask what happened next.
